title: Lua
subtitle: Lua scripts make the Redis control plane's job promotion atomic and keep the broker's hot-path bookkeeping on the server.

stats.label: lines of Lua, loaded by hash

lede: The FAFO Core and Function Forge control plane keeps job state in Redis, and many workers change that state at once. A Redis pipeline batches commands without making them atomic, and a crash or a competing worker between two commands leaves a job half-updated. I moved every multi-step state change onto the server as a Lua script. Job promotion is one script: it moves a job from pending to processing and writes the job's worker count, batch size and batch mode in the same step, so no worker ever sees a half-promoted job.
quote: I find the places where distributed state can tear and close them at the server.
evidence: Redis Lua scripting: 16 server-side scripts of about 4,000 lines making multi-step job state changes atomic.
Distributed systems correctness: scripts that return the state they produced, removing read-after-write races from every caller.
Workload isolation: 3 Redis instances split by role so a write backlog cannot starve job control.
author: Corey James
